name: Teleportation requires 2 classical bits per qubit; without them B is maximally mixed (Bennett, Brassard, Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres & Wootters, PRL 70, 1895 (1993); lower bound as restated by Bennett et al. 2001 and proved for exact schemes by Werner 2001)

source.located: Primary: C.H. Bennett, G. Brassard, C. Crepeau, R. Jozsa, A. Peres, W.K. Wootters, 'Teleporting an unknown quantum state via dual classical and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen channels', Phys. Rev. Lett. 70, 1895 (1993) -- pre-quant-ph, no arXiv copy; NAMED-NOT-READ in itself. Restatements READ at alphaXiv: (i) S. Pirandola, J. Eisert, C. Weedbrook, A. Furusawa, S.L. Braunstein, 'Advances in quantum teleportation', arXiv:1505.07831v1 pp.1-2 (protocol, hypotheses); (ii) C.H. Bennett, D.P. DiVincenzo, P.W. Shor, J.A. Smolin, B.M. Terhal, W.K. Wootters, 'Remote State Preparation', arXiv:quant-ph/0006044v5 (PRL 87, 077902 (2001)) p.1 (the necessity statement); (iii) R.F. Werner, 'All teleportation and dense coding schemes', arXiv:quant-ph/0003070v1 (J. Phys. A 34, 7081 (2001)) Thm 1 and its corollary pp.5-7 (the d^2 lower bound for exact schemes, proved).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1505.07831, quant-ph/0003070, quant-ph/0006044 (page text returned and read). Bennett 1993 itself is NAMED-NOT-READ: every statement attributed to it below is quoted from these restatements, which name it as their ref. [2]/[BB]/[1].

published_statement: Protocol (Pirandola et al. 2015 restating Bennett et al. 1993, p.1-2): Alice and Bob 'share two qubits, A and B, prepared in a pure entangled state. In the ideal case, this is taken to be maximally entangled ... At the input, Alice is given another qubit a whose state rho is unknown. She then performs ... Bell detection, which projects her qubits a and A into one of the four Bell states (P_k x I)|Phi>, k = 0..3 ... Bob's qubit B is simultaneously projected onto P_k^dag rho P_k. In the last (feed-forward) step ... Alice communicates the classical outcome k ... to Bob, who then applies P_k to recover the original input state rho. Note that Alice's input state is assumed to be unknown, otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation.' 'This process requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication.' NECESSITY (Bennett et al. 2001, p.1): 'Two bits of forward classical communication and one ebit of entanglement ... per teleported qubit are both necessary and sufficient, and neither resource can be traded off against the other.' EXACT-SCHEME BOUND (Werner 2001, pp.6-7): 'teleportation ... schemes exist whenever n >= d^2 ... The optimality of these dimension inequalities, i.e. that no teleportation ... scheme exists with n < d^2 ... is also a corollary of Theorem 1' (n = number of classical signals, d = input dimension, resource on H(d) x H(d)); any tight scheme has a pure maximally entangled resource, unitary corrections and a complete von Neumann measurement.
published_hypotheses: H1 the input state is UNKNOWN to the sender (arbitrary; may be part of a larger entangled system) -- 'otherwise the protocol reduces to remote state preparation' (1505.07831 p.2)

H2 resource: one pure MAXIMALLY entangled pair per qubit for exact (F = 1) teleportation; a partially entangled pure two-qubit resource gives perfect teleportation 'if and only if' maximally entangled (2506.18577 p.2, citing Li-Li-Guo 2000)
H3 a complete (four-outcome) Bell measurement; with incomplete Bell detection the protocol is post-selected/probabilistic (1505.07831 p.4)

H4 the 'necessary' 2 bits: for exact single-shot schemes with a d x d resource, n >= d^2 signals (Werner Thm 1 corollary: 'tight' case, all Hilbert spaces dimension d); as an asymptotic rate, 2 cbits per qubit even with any amount of prior entanglement ('neither resource can be traded off', 0006044 p.1)

H5 forward classical communication only; the bits travel on an ordinary classical channel -- the '<= c' of that channel is relativity, not part of the theorem (the theorem states only that classical communication is required, hence 'excludes superluminal communication')
H6 ordinary (linear) quantum mechanics: no-signalling of local operations on a shared state (the no-communication theorem)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (H1, unknown input), transit.py:140 'CLASSICAL_BITS_PER_QUBIT = 2' with selftest label 'classical bits required per qubit' (transit.py:335) and transit.py:37-39 / 209-210 'The state does not exist at the far end until two classical bits arrive': the 2-bit REQUIREMENT is a theorem for an UNKNOWN (arbitrary) input. For a state the sender KNOWS classically (remote state preparation), the asymptotic cost is ONE bit per qubit (Bennett et al. 2001, quant-ph/0006044 p.1: 'the asymptotic classical communication cost of RSP is one bit per qubit -- half that of teleportation'), and for known equatorial states one bit suffices EXACTLY (Pati 1999, restated there; re-derived here, N3: fidelity 1.000000000000000 with one bit). The tree's 'object in transition' (transit.py:57-60) does not say whether its state is known to the sender. The count 2 is therefore narrowed; the refusal it feeds is not (see lacked_data / grade): RSP still needs >= 1 bit per qubit 'by causality' (0006044 p.2), and B's averaged state without the bit is still I/2 (N3, deviation 5.6e-16).

DROPPED (H4, derivation), transit.py:140 and :335: the lower bound is HARD-CODED and the selftest checks the constant against itself (chk('classical bits required per qubit', CLASSICAL_BITS_PER_QUBIT, 2)) -- a tautology, not a derivation. The number is nevertheless CORRECT under H1-H3: re-derived here (N1) by the reference-system argument I(R;B_out) <= I(R;B) + H(M) <= 0 + log2 k, with exact teleportation requiring I(R;B_out) = 2, so k >= 4; the standard protocol saturates it (I(R;BM) = 2.000000000000, H(M) = 2.000000000000), and coarse-grained Bell schemes with k = 3 and k = 2 reach only 1.5 and 1.0 bits (N2). Werner 2001's corollary proves the same n >= d^2 for exact schemes. The drift is in the tree's EVIDENCE for the number, not the number.

NARROWED IN WORDING (H2), entry name 'without them B is maximally mixed' and transit.py:37 'B's state is EXACTLY I/2': 'exactly I/2' requires the maximally entangled resource. With a non-maximal resource c0|00>+c1|11> the no-bits average is diag(c0^2, c1^2) (sympy S2), NOT I/2 -- but still independent of the input, so 'ZERO INFORMATION' holds for every resource. The tree's own protocol uses a Bell pair (transit.py:89), so for the tree's instance 'exactly I/2' is correct; only the general reading of the sentence overreaches.

OVERSTATED (interpretive), transit.py:38-39 / 209-210 and paper/CLAIMS.md:4620 'The state does not exist at the far end until two classical bits arrive': what the theorem gives is that B's state AVERAGED over Alice's unknown outcome is input-independent (I/2 here) and carries zero information; conditioned on the outcome, B's qubit IS in the state P_k^dag rho P_k (1505.07831 p.2; S1 here: each branch is sigma_m psi exactly). 'Does not exist' is an interpretation of 'B cannot know which branch'; recorded as a discrepancy of description, not of number.

ADDED (H5 is imported, and correctly flagged by the canonical entry), transit.py:38-39 'through ordinary space at <= c' and :138-141 arrival_time(D) = D/C_SI: the <= c is relativistic causality, not part of Bennett et al. The ledger quantity advantage_over_light(D) = arrival_time(D) - D/C_SI (transit.py:141) is IDENTICALLY 0 by definition (sympy N4: D/c - D/c = 0) -- the four '0.000' rows (transit.py:246-251, selftest :340-341) restate the <= c hypothesis; they are not a measurement against light. index3.py:1366 ('THE ADVANTAGE IS 0.000 ... PROVABLY SO, because the no-communication theorem is a theorem') is right that the refusal is proved, but the proof is no-communication + '<= c for the classical channel', not the 1000-trial number.

FAITHFUL, transit.py:129-136 b_state_without_bits: averages p_m |v_m><v_m| over the four outcomes with corrections withheld -- exactly the quantity whose input-independence the theorem asserts; sympy S1 gives rho_B = [[1/2,0],[0,1/2]] EXACTLY for symbolic (a,b), so the report's 1.1e-16 (transit.py:37) and the selftest's < 1e-14 (:332) are double-precision rounding of an exact zero (N4: max 3.33e-16 over 1000 inputs).
FAITHFUL, transit.py:113-126 teleport(): four outcomes, p = 1/4 each, Pauli corrections I, X, Z, ZX restore psi exactly -- confirmed symbolically (S1).

data_at_publication.quantity: deviation of rho_B (no bits) from I/2
data_at_publication.value_now: exactly 0 (sympy, symbolic input a|0>+b|1> with |a|^2+|b|^2=1); 3.33e-16 max over 1000 random inputs in float64
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: no -- the tree's number is rounding of an exact identity; the conclusion is strengthened, not moved

data_at_publication.value_then: tree: 2, hard-coded (transit.py:140), no derivation; Bennett et al. 1993 protocol uses 2
data_at_publication.value_now: 2 is the proved minimum for exact teleportation of an UNKNOWN qubit (Werner 2001 n >= d^2; reference-system bound re-derived N1, saturated); asymptotically 2 even with unlimited entanglement (0006044). For KNOWN states: 1 bit/qubit asymptotically (RSP, 0006044), 1 bit exactly for equatorial states (Pati 1999, N3); lower bound 1 bit/qubit by causality
data_at_publication.source_now: arXiv:quant-ph/0003070 Thm 1 corollary; arXiv:quant-ph/0006044 p.1-2; rederive N1-N3
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: moves the COUNT for known-state transfer (2 -> 1); does NOT move the refusal: any protocol still needs >= 1 classical bit per qubit and B holds zero information before it arrives, so the arrival time is still >= D/c under H5

data_at_publication.quantity: c (the classical channel's speed; enters only through H5)
data_at_publication.source_now: SI definition (1983, retained in the 2019 SI); not a measured datum

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0, ~1 s). S1 (sympy, exact): for symbolic input a|0>+b|1>, each Bell outcome has p = 1/4, Pauli corrections restore psi exactly, and the no-bits average is rho_B = I/2 exactly, input-independent. S2 (sympy): with resource cos(t)|00>+sin(t)|11> the no-bits average is diag(cos^2 t, sin^2 t) -- input-independent (zero information) but NOT I/2 unless maximally entangled. N1 (numeric): reference-system lower bound -- I(R;B) = 8.9e-16 before any message, exact teleportation needs I(R;B_out) = 2.000 on every branch, and I(R;BM) <= log2 k for a k-valued classical message, so k >= 4 (2 bits); the standard protocol saturates it, I(R;BM) = H(M) = 2.000000000000. N2: coarse-grained Bell schemes k = 3, 2 reach I(R;BM) = 1.5, 1.0 (< 2, <= log2 k); 200 random k-outcome protocols each for k = 2,3,4 respect the bound (sanity check only; random search does not probe the extremal region). N3: remote state preparation of KNOWN equatorial states with ONE bit, min fidelity 1.000000000000000 over 50 states, and B without the bit is I/2 (dev 5.6e-16). N4: transit.py's no-bits deviation is float rounding (3.33e-16 max over 1000 inputs); advantage_over_light(D) = D/c - D/c = 0 by definition. The inequality chain in N1 (data processing under Bob's local map; I(R;M|B) <= H(M|B) <= log2 k because M is classical) is a proof, not a numeric fit; N2 only exercises it.

later_literature.ref: R.F. Werner, 'All teleportation and dense coding schemes', arXiv:quant-ph/0003070 (J. Phys. A 34, 7081 (2001))
later_literature.what: Proves (Thm 1 + corollary) that no exact teleportation scheme of a d-level system with a d x d resource uses fewer than d^2 classical signals, and that every tight scheme has a pure maximally entangled resource, unitary corrections and a complete von Neumann measurement. For d = 2: 4 signals = 2 bits. Supplies the derivation the tree hard-codes.

later_literature.ref: C.H. Bennett, D.P. DiVincenzo, P.W. Shor, J.A. Smolin, B.M. Terhal, W.K. Wootters, 'Remote State Preparation', arXiv:quant-ph/0006044 (PRL 87, 077902 (2001))
later_literature.what: States the teleportation necessity (2 cbits + 1 ebit per qubit, neither tradeable) and shows that for a KNOWN state the asymptotic classical cost is 1 bit per qubit (with large prior entanglement), lower-bounded at 1 bit 'by causality'; Lo's conjecture (2 log d for exact finite-n RSP) proved only for oblivious, unitary-correction, exactly faithful protocols. Narrows the tree's '2 bits per qubit' to unknown inputs; leaves the no-FTL conclusion intact.

later_literature.ref: S. Pirandola, J. Eisert, C. Weedbrook, A. Furusawa, S.L. Braunstein, 'Advances in quantum teleportation', arXiv:1505.07831 (Nature Photon. 9, 641 (2015))
later_literature.what: Restates the 1993 protocol with its hypotheses (unknown input, maximally entangled resource ideally, complete Bell detection), 'requires classical communication and excludes superluminal communication'; d^2 signals for d-level DV schemes; port-based teleportation needs no correction but fidelity -> 1 only as the number of ports (log2 n bits) grows; lists experiments with real-time feed-forward to 143 km.

later_literature.ref: D. Zhu, J.-L. Chen, F.-L. Zhang, 'Classical and Quantum Resources in Perfect Teleportation', arXiv:2506.18577 (2025)
later_literature.what: Perfect qubit teleportation through partially entangled two-qutrit channels; the Shannon entropy of the classical message is >= 2 bits, reaching its lower bound of 2 bits only when the channel reduces to a two-qubit Bell state (H12 = 2.5 in their theta1 = pi/4 case). Consistent with 2 as the floor for an unknown qubit; perfect teleportation with a partially entangled TWO-QUBIT resource is impossible (their Sec. II, citing Li-Li-Guo 2000).

later_literature.ref: Sohail, A.K. Pati, V. Aradhya, I. Chakrabarty, S. Patro, 'Teleportation of quantum coherence', arXiv:2302.11499 (2023)
later_literature.what: Perfect teleportation of even the l1-coherence of an ARBITRARY unknown qubit with one cbit is impossible; one cbit suffices only for partially known states (equatorial / polar circles). Restates 'teleportation of an unknown state is possible with ... two classical bits' and RSP's one bit for equatorial states.

later_literature.ref: A.K. Pati, quant-ph/9907022; H.-K. Lo, quant-ph/9912009 (RSP for special ensembles; Lo's conjecture)
later_literature.what: One bit suffices for known equatorial states (Pati); Lo conjectured equal costs for general states. Used here only as restated in quant-ph/0006044 p.1-2; the equatorial one-bit protocol is re-derived numerically (N3).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: 'previous physicists may have all lacked certain data'. Bennett et al. 1993 is a THEOREM of finite-dimensional quantum mechanics; its conclusion depends on NO measured datum (the tree's only numbers are a float-rounding residual, an integer, and c, which is exact by SI definition). What was not in hand in 1993 and came later: (a) the proof of optimality for exact schemes (Werner 2001) -- it CONFIRMS 2 bits for an unknown qubit; (b) remote state preparation (Pati 1999, Lo 1999, Bennett et al. 2001) -- it LOWERS the cost to 1 bit per qubit when the sender knows the state, which is a genuine narrowing of the '2', found later; (c) experiments with real-time feed-forward (restated in 1505.07831: 16 km free space, 143 km, atomic and solid-state deterministic teleportation) -- none reports an arrival without the classical message. Evidence either way: the later knowledge changes the COUNT for known inputs (2 -> 1), and changes nothing about the refusal the tree builds on it, because the refusal needs only (i) no-signalling -- B's averaged state is input-independent without the message, re-derived exactly here for every resource (S1, S2) and for RSP (N3) -- and (ii) the classical channel being <= c (H5, relativity, audited under the c entry). A data change would have to break linear quantum mechanics' no-signalling; no datum in the literature read here does that, and none is presumed.
grade_evidence: The theorem is right where it is stated and the tree's instance is reproduced exactly: sympy S1 gives rho_B = I/2 identically for a symbolic input (the tree's 1.1e-16 is rounding), four outcomes at p = 1/4, fidelity 1 after Pauli corrections. The number 2 is re-derived as a lower bound (N1: I(R;B_out) = 2 requires log2 k >= 2; saturated by the standard protocol) and matches Werner 2001's proved n >= d^2. The NARROWING: (1) the tree states '2 classical bits required per qubit' (transit.py:140, :335) without the hypothesis H1 that the input is UNKNOWN to the sender; for known states remote state preparation needs 1 bit per qubit asymptotically (quant-ph/0006044) and exactly 1 for equatorial states (re-derived, N3); (2) 'exactly I/2' needs the maximally entangled resource (S2: diag(c0^2, c1^2) otherwise), though 'zero information' holds for every resource. Neither narrowing reaches the conclusion the tree rests on it (transit.py 'advantage 0', D23/R11/Rec): every protocol, including RSP, still needs >= 1 classical bit whose absence leaves B input-independent. Also recorded, not graded: the 2-bit selftest check is a tautology (constant vs itself), advantage_over_light is 0 by definition (N4), and 'the state does not exist at the far end' overstates 'B cannot know which branch'. Not WRONG: nothing refutes the source; not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum enters.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names H1 at transit.py:140/:335 (e.g. 'for an UNKNOWN input; 1 bit/qubit for a known state via RSP, still >= 1 by causality') and the maximally-entangled hypothesis for 'exactly I/2' -- or shows that its use case requires an unknown input state. To WRONG: an exact scheme for arbitrary unknown qubits with fewer than 4 classical signals (would contradict Werner Thm 1 and the N1 inequality chain), or an exhibited protocol in which B's no-message state depends on the input (a violation of no-signalling). To DATA-DEPENDENT: an experiment showing input-dependence of B's state before the classical message arrives -- none is known in the literature read here. Reading Bennett et al. 1993 itself (PRL 70, 1895) would upgrade the read status from READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT; it is not expected to move the grade.
